specification_purpose: Preregister the rules for a fourth, separately versioned market-cap universe that is a strictly additional batch of assets below the v3 universe floor. This file is a design artifact: it freezes rules before any v4 data is retrieved or any v4 result exists, and it authorizes nothing.

sections_implemented_here: BRAIN-013 recommendation 1: preregister the new version and its retrieval window first
BRAIN-013 recommendation 2: retrieve exactly one market-cap snapshot inside the pinned window
BRAIN-013 recommendation 3: validate every candidate against real provider data
BRAIN-013 recommendation 4: separate namespaces for every version
BRAIN-013 recommendation 4: extend identity rule to v1,v2,v3
BRAIN-013 recommendation 6: inherit the strategy grid, costs, folds and selection rule unchanged

supersedes.reason: The v3 universe is frozen, its selection run has been performed and its confirmatory window is single-use. The v4 universe is a strictly additional batch of assets below the v3 universe floor, so it supersedes the v3 universe only in the sense that it is the program's current universe version.
supersedes.supersession_scope: Additive only. The v1, v2 and v3 artifacts are not replaced, rewritten or reinterpreted: they remain immutable historical evidence, and the v4 candidate set contains no asset of any of them.

hashing.note: The specification_hash binds every other field of this file, including created_utc. Recomputing it over the parsed document with the key removed is the only accepted verification.

inheritance.statement: v4 changes the evaluated universe only. The strategy family, the 2,304-configuration grid, cost assumptions, execution semantics, fold structure, selection rule, pilot gate, metrics, baselines and status vocabulary are inherited from v1 without modification, and the data retrieval contract is inherited from v2 without modification, so that v4 differs from v3 in which assets are evaluated and not in how a strategy is measured.

universe.survivorship_disclaimer: Current-universe snapshot used; historical point-in-time ranks unavailable. Results have survivorship limitations.

expansion_scope.rule: The v4 universe is the next batch below the recorded floor: assets of a fresh market-cap snapshot whose market capitalization is strictly below the floor and that are not assets of the v1, v2, or v3 universe.

prior_universe_floor.recompute_rule: the floor is the minimum market_cap_usd over the eligible_assets of research/universe_manifest_v3.json; the verifier recomputes it from that manifest and never trusts this recorded value
prior_universe_floor.note: The v4 batch contains only assets that a fresh, deeper ranking places below the market capitalization of the lowest asset that universe version v3 evaluated. The v3 universe itself is not re-ranked, widened or narrowed.

prior_universe_asset_identity.rule: An asset is 'already in a prior universe' when its Binance symbol or its CoinGecko id already occurs in the eligible assets of the v1, v2, or v3 universe manifest.
prior_universe_asset_identity.rename_rule: A renamed asset keeps its CoinGecko id and is therefore the same asset; it is excluded from the v4 batch as already_in_prior_universe.

expansion_scope.ordering_rule: Candidates are taken in strictly descending market-capitalization order after the prior-universe and exclusion rules have been applied; the batch contains exactly top_n assets unless the snapshot runs out of eligible names, in which case the shortfall is recorded.

snapshot_retrieval.rule: The v4 universe is exactly one timestamped market-cap snapshot retrieved inside the window below. The first successful retrieval inside the window is the v4 snapshot.

holdout.development_data_cutoff_note: BRAIN-013: any development data read at or after v3 window open is inside v3 confirmatory window; v4 development data bounded at cutoff with cost noted.

v4_confirmatory_window.rule: A fresh, unexposed confirmatory window evaluated only after the v3 candidate manifest is frozen and hash-bound.
v4_confirmatory_window.min_hours_rationale: 90 days of closed hourly candles; the v1 protocol used a 0.2 holdout fraction of a multi-year window, which is of the same order.
v4_confirmatory_window.access_counting: Every read of a candle inside the v3 confirmatory window increments holdout_exposed_count in the v3 checkpoint and is recorded in the v3 holdout report.
v4_confirmatory_window.not_a_v1_or_v2_holdout: This is a new protocol object, not a re-opening of the v1 final holdout or of the v2 confirmatory window. It is never populated with data that predates the v3 candidate freeze.

v3_confirmatory_window.rule: A fresh, unexposed confirmatory window evaluated only after the v3 candidate manifest is frozen and hash-bound.
v3_confirmatory_window.min_hours_rationale: 90 days of closed hourly candles; the v1 protocol used a 0.2 holdout fraction of a multi-year window, which is of the same order.
v3_confirmatory_window.access_counting: Every read of a candle inside the v3 confirmatory window increments holdout_exposed_count in the v3 checkpoint and is recorded in the v3 holdout report.
v3_confirmatory_window.not_a_v1_or_v2_holdout: This is a new protocol object, not a re-opening of the v1 final holdout or of the v2 confirmatory window. It is never populated with data that predates the v3 candidate freeze.

v2_confirmatory_window.note: The v2 confirmatory window is single-use evidence for the v2 candidate set and cannot exist before 2027-01-17T22:00:00Z. A v3 expansion never reads it, re-times it, reuses it or extends it (BRAIN-012 D-3), and the v2 holdout exposure counter is not touched by any v3 artifact.

comparability.rule: v4 differs only in the universe. The grid, costs, execution, folds, selection rule and single confirmatory criterion are identical to v1.

authorization.reason: This specification authorizes nothing. All authorizations require separate, hash-bound artifacts and must not begin before their time gates.

data.failover_policy: One bounded request to the primary host. If it fails (for example HTTP 451), use the documented failover host and record both statuses with timestamps. The primary host is failed over, not blindly retried. max_retries applies to transient failures on the active endpoint only.
